paraphrase: (The Lord says:) I alone am full of all qualities; my designator is the praṇava, which, from 'a' to 'atiśānta', is eightfold; it designates my forms Viśva, Taijasa, Prājña, Turīya, Ātman, Antarātman, Paramātman and Jñānātman.
speaker: the Lord (as reported by Madhva)
notes: checked against the Devanāgarī e-text in sources_raw/raw_etexts/vedAntam/dvaitam (github.com/sanskrit/raw_etexts); numbering follows that copy and may differ in other editions

paraphrase: The Lord has fifty further forms, designated by the fifty letters as differentiated from the praṇava — Aja, Ānanda, Indra, Īśa, Ugra, Ūrja, Ṛtambhara and the rest down to the last; from the praṇava arise the eight-syllable Nārāyaṇa mantra, the vyāhṛtis, the twelve-syllable mantra with the Keśava forms as its deities, and the Gāyatrī.
speaker: the Lord (as reported by Madhva)
notes: Verses 5–10 list the fifty forms; 11–14 the derived mantras. checked against the Devanāgarī e-text in sources_raw/raw_etexts/vedAntam/dvaitam (github.com/sanskrit/raw_etexts); numbering follows that copy and may differ in other editions
